notes: Both coders found the same two documents (Academic Affairs guidance PDF; Academic Integrity and Generative AI hub page) and gave both the stance delegates. Main disagreements: (1) policy type for rationale or context sentences (opening 'valuable tool' P56 vs P87; 'concern about misuse' P56 vs UNCOVERED; penalty factors UNCOVERED vs P37; Student Care Network P72 vs UNCOVERED), resolved by re-reading the sentence and choosing the type whose definition it states, keeping UNCOVERED where no type fit; (2) modality of soft advice (may vs should vs informs), resolved from the source verb; (3) phase (general vs before-course/during-work) for rationale and motivation sentences. Unit granularity differed in the hub page: coder A split heading plus body and individual red flags, coder B folded some, so most only-A units (11 kept, 1 dropped: the warning-letter template link, which is a resource link not a rule) are real list items; coder B-only units kept (4 of 7) are separate sentences A missed, and the other 3 B-only units were merged into A units that cover the same rule. One pair (A 'reports of unauthorized AI use' with B 'Is supported by factors') was matched by hand because the anchors sat more than 60 characters apart.
